Assets

Operational sites mount on turbines. Pre-construction sites have none, so the units go on whatever the survey put up: a scaffold tower, a pole, the cabin roof. Proposed places a consented turbine position with no turbine on it, drawn with its future rotor sweep so coverage can be assessed against the layout that is coming.

Detection & classification range

px/m at range is the ground resolution at the zone's working distance; px on target is what that leaves across the bird itself. Detection needs about ${DET}, a stable track ${TRK}, and species-level classification ${CLS}. At night the reach of the Raytec panels caps everything: see Method.

Rotor geometry assessed

The rotor-swept sphere is the notional volume that triggers an interaction event. The sub-geometry is the finer volume tested for blade encounter: a torus follows the blade sweep annulus, a plane treats the whole rotor disc.

Method

How stereo works The same bird, the same instant, two cameras, one 3D track
drag the lower panel to orbit
True path
Reconstructed
Sightline A
Sightline B
Uncertainty, true scale
A camera gives a direction, not a distance. Two cameras on the same bird at the same instant give two directions, and where those lines meet is the bird. Everything below follows from the angle between them.
Move the second camera
90°
Nothing about the cameras changes, only where the second one stands. Bring the two into line and the reconstruction stretches along the sightline.
Measurement noise
1.5 px
Each camera also carries a 1.2 mrad alignment residual, about 0.07°, which calibration leaves behind and averaging cannot remove. The geometry amplifies it exactly as it amplifies pixel noise.
